title: taproot kv heuristic scratch - soren
content:
AM: quick brain dump before standup — focus: KV cache eviction heuristics that might explain yesterday's p99 spike on small seq lengths. TL;DR: suspect cross-model evictions + small-batch pathological pattern when prefix reuse low.

Observations:
- Spike at ~10:23 UTC yesterday, correlated with burst of short requests (avg seq 24 tokens) from hosted-api (route: /v1/completions, model: rwkv-1b-3q).
- Cache hit rate fell from 87% -> 32% for that minute on node gpu-7.
- Eviction logs show repeated churn: same key prefixes inserted then evicted within <200ms windows.
- Autoscaler added 1 pod; latency improved but unit cost jumped.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Tiny-sequence churn: many distinct prompts with low prefix overlap cause frequent small-key writes; LRU favors new short-lived entries, thrashing cache.
2) Cross-model key collision: model variants share the same namespace for KV keys; small seq keys are shorter and collide at higher rate.
3) Background GC job (metadata compaction) triggered on that node causing transient stall, reducing effective cache capacity.

Quick checks to run (today):
- Reproduce locally: replay trace from hosted logs (INF-2147) against dev runtime with kv-cache debug enabled. Command: ./bin/replay --trace infra/traces/2026-03-09/gpu-7-10-23.trace --kv-debug
- Add verbose eviction reason to runtime logs for a 5-minute window on staging; filter for keys <= 48 bytes.
- Run small batch microbench: 1000 requests, seq len 20-30, concurrency 50, two model variants; compare hit/miss and eviction churn.

Quick TODOs (who/when):
- [Soren] instrument eviction reasons + short-key tagging on staging (by EOD 2026-03-12).
- [Mina] export hosted request sample and produce prefix-uniqueness histogram (INF-2147 follow-up) (tomorrow AM).
- [Hector] confirm K/V namespace partitioning per-model in runtime code and sketch mitigation (namespace salts) (Wednesday).

Mitigations to try (low-risk, fast):
- Treat keys shorter than 64 bytes as "short-lived" and place them in a small LRU partition capped at 5% of cache. Expected: reduce thrash on main partition. Risk: may lower hit rate for genuinely reusable short prefixes.
- Add probabilistic admission for new entries when cache eviction rate > threshold (reject small keys with P=0.6). Fast to toggle via flag.
- Namespace salt per model variant (longer-term, needs migration).

Notes for PR / tickets:
- Add test that simulates tiny-seq churn and asserts eviction rate delta after short-key partition applied. Put under runtime/kv/tests/eviction_sim.cc and reference INF-2147.
- Link PR to serving-runtime PR 4321 (work-in-progress patch for short-key tagging).

Questions for standup:
- Are we comfortable shipping short-key partition behind a feature flag? Service teams can enable for specific routes.
- If autoscaler responds to latency but drives cost up, do we prefer temporary capacity overshoot or more conservative scaling with fallback to a cheaper model variant?

Misc scratch (commands, quick diffs):
- grep -n "evict_reason" runtime/ -R | head
- local replay script: python tools/replay.py --input traces/gpu-7-2026-03-09.json --concurrency 50 --model rwkv-1b-3q --kv-log
- quick metric snapshot:
  p50: 6ms, p95: 28ms, p99: 410ms (10:23-10:24)
  kv hit-rate: 32% (same minute)

Later notes (post 12:00):
- Mina sent prefix histogram: 73% of short requests have unique first-3 tokens. Supports hypothesis #1.
- Hector confirmed namespace salt not applied for model aliases; adding minimal salt (variant id) reduced collisions in sim by ~7%.

Next actions: land eviction-reason instrumentation -> run staging experiments -> consider enabling short-key partition behind flag on a low-traffic route for 24h A/B test.

Random reminders: file bug with infra to retain gpu metrics for 7d (we currently only have 48h); ping infra@redwood.

End of scratch.
